name: rental
description: Car rental agency: vehicles by class at branches, one-way rentals, mileage allowances, late returns, damage deposits and invoices.
author: test3 author (rental)

issues.description: The docstring says every started 24-hour period is a whole day (24h01 is two days), but floor division drops the started day, so 25 hours bills one day and late returns lose their partial days.
issues.fix_hint: Round up: count the whole days and add one when there is a remainder, keeping the minimum of one day.

issues.description: late_days takes (due_at, returned_at) but is called with the return time first, so late returns are never charged and early returns are charged as late.

The extras default is a shared list and the young-driver surcharge is appended to it, so every later contract opened without extras carries the young-driver charge (and the contract keeps a reference to the caller's list).
issues.fix_hint: Default to None and work on a fresh copy: extras = list(extras or []).

issues.description: The docstring and README say only a manager of the drop-off branch may waive damage, but only the branch is checked, so any counter agent there can cancel a damage charge.
issues.fix_hint: Raise PermissionError unless staff.is_manager, in addition to the branch check.

issues.description: contracts imports invoice to bill a returned contract and invoice imports contracts for the day counting rules; the two modules depend on each other and only work because each uses the other lazily.
The 14% sales tax rate is written as a bare literal twice (0.14 in Invoice.tax and 1.14 in quote) instead of one named constant next to the rate card; changing the rate means finding both.
The private helper _periods_overlap is never called anywhere in the package.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: It iterates over a list copy of the items, so deleting from the dict inside the loop is safe.
The grace period is inclusive by the docstring and README: a car back exactly 59 minutes after it was due is on time.
